description: The selected item is the subject.
The selected item is the direct object.
The selected item is the indirect object, typically a recipient.
A non-subject argument selected by this entry, contributing its own lexical content. 'rumour that he left'. For an adposition or affix that only marks a role, use 'case marking'.
An argument whose more specific relation is not being distinguished.
This entry adds a property to the selected item. Adjective-noun, adverb-verb, and adjuncts. Not determiners or numerals — see 'determination' and 'quantification'.
An optional non-selected dependent, when you want it distinguished from modification.
A non-core argument of this entry, often case- or adposition-marked. This is the ARGUMENT's relation to its verb; for the marker's own relation to what it marks, use 'case marking'.
The selected item is the possessor.
This entry fixes the reference of the selected item — definiteness, deixis or specificity. Determiner-noun: 'the dog', 'this dog'. Adds no property, so it is not modification.
This entry specifies the quantity or amount of the selected item. Numeral- or quantifier-noun: 'three dogs', 'many dogs'.

This entry marks the grammatical role of the selected item without contributing lexical content of its own. Case-marking adpositions, clitics and affixes. Contrast 'complement', where the adposition has its own meaning.
This entry joins the selected item into a larger structure — subordinator, complementizer or coordinator.
